Understanding How Guardian Labs Labels Funded Content

Transparency in Digital Journalism

In the modern media landscape, news organizations utilize diverse revenue streams to maintain operations. The Guardian, a prominent news outlet, maintains specific protocols for content produced with support from outside parties. These arrangements ensure that readers can distinguish between standard editorial journalism and material that is financially supported by third-party funders.

Four Key Labels

To ensure clarity, the publication employs four distinct labels to inform readers about the nature of the content they are consuming:

  • Supported by: This label identifies content that remains editorially independent. While third parties, such as commercial clients or philanthropic foundations, provide funding, the commissioning and final editorial control remain with Guardian staff. Clients may suggest topics, but journalists are not obligated to follow these suggestions, and funders do not preview or approve the copy before publication.
  • Advertising partner / Exclusive advertising partner: Specifically used by Guardian US, this label denotes editorially independent content funded by commercial partners. It functions similarly to the "Supported by" category but is explicitly reserved for commercial, rather than philanthropic, funding sources.
  • Paid content / Paid for by: This designation refers to advertisement features. Unlike editorial content, this material is controlled by the advertiser rather than the publisher. It is subject to regulatory standards such as those set by the Federal Trade Commission in the US, the Advertising Standards Authority in the UK, and the Advertising Standards Bureau in Australia.
  • Advertiser content / from our advertisers: Similar to the previous category, this label indicates content both paid for and produced entirely by the advertiser. It is hosted by the platform but does not involve Guardian journalists or editorial staff.

Impact on the Reader

These labeling standards serve to provide transparency regarding the influence behind the information presented. By distinguishing between content produced by journalists and content originating from advertisers, the publication aims to preserve the integrity of its independent reporting while acknowledging the financial realities of contemporary media production.

Readers who wish to understand the specific ethical guidelines and disclosure policies regarding this funded content can review the official documentation provided by the organization.

How to Verify

To view the original source regarding these editorial policies and to see a list of current philanthropic projects supported by external foundations, visit the official page here: https://www.theguardian.com/info/2016/jan/25/content-funding.
